chunks: Ahmad narrated from Amr ibn Uthman from Ali ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'O group of those who have not performed Hajj, receive glad tidings with the pilgrs, shake their hands, and magnify them, for that is obligatory upon you so that you may share with them in the reward.'
ai.seo_question: What should those who did not perform Hajj do to share in the reward of the pilgrims?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) instructs those who could not perform Hajj to rejoice in the success of the pilgrims, shake their hands, and honor them, as this act is obligatory and allows them to share in the pilgrims' reward. This narration highlights the Shia concept of *shirkah fi al-ajr* (sharing in reward), where the spiritual merit of Hajj extends to the community through the recognition and celebration of those who performed it, reinforcing social cohesion and collective piety.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad, from Amro Bin Isman, from Ali Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘O group of the ones who did not perform Hajj! Receive glad tidings with the pilgrims, and shake their hands, and magnify them, for that is Obligatory upon you in order to participate with them in the Recompense’.
en.sarwar: 47. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that one who normally attends al-Hajj every year, then he lags behind and does not go for al-Hajj one year, the angels on land say to those in the mountains, ‘We miss hearing the voice of so and so.’ They then say, ‘Allow us to search for him.’ They search but do not find him and they say, “O Allah, if debts have kept him behind, pay them off for him; if illness has kept him from performing, grant him good health; if it is poverty, grant him wealth; if it is prison, grant him freedom; if a preoccupation, please complete it for him.’” People pray for themselves; they (angels) pray for those who have remained behind.’”
